details: The US Personal Consumption Expenditures (PCE) price index, the Federal Reserve's preferred inflation gauge, registered a softer-than-expected increase in August 2026. The headline PCE rose 3.4% year-on-year, while the core PCE (excluding volatile food and energy components) increased by 3.0%. Both figures were below market forecasts, leading to a notable reduction in the probability of a Fed interest rate hike at its upcoming October 28th meeting. This softer inflation data initially saw Bitcoin's price surge past $85,000.
title: US Inflation Eases, Reducing Immediate Fed Hike Odds

details: Following the recent inflation report, the market-implied probability of a Federal Reserve interest rate hike at its October 28th meeting has dropped to below 50%. Despite this, the benchmark 10-year US Treasury yield continues to hover near multi-decade highs, creating a persistent headwind for risk assets, including cryptocurrencies, which do not offer a yield. While some Fed officials maintain that further policy adjustments may be necessary, a "no urgency" stance for an immediate hike has also been voiced.
title: Fed Rate Hike Probability Declines for October, But Yields Remain High

details: 2026 is being recognized as a pivotal year for digital asset adoption, marked by significant strides in institutional integration and regulatory clarity. The Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) has officially launched its tokenization service, which is now being utilized by major financial players such as BlackRock, Goldman Sachs, and JPMorgan. Concurrently, the US SEC has proposed a new "Regulation Crypto Assets" framework, designed to offer definitive legal exemptions for companies issuing digital tokens and facilitate fundraising for crypto projects. Further regulatory news includes Illinois postponing its crypto transaction tax until July 2027 and Latvia issuing its first MiCA crypto license.
title: Institutional Adoption and Regulatory Clarity Advance Digital Assets

details: The European Central Bank (ECB) is scheduled to hold its next monetary policy meeting on October 28-29, 2026, with the interest rate decision expected on October 29th. The Euro area's flash inflation estimate for August 2026 stood at 3.2% year-on-year, remaining above the ECB's 2% target. ECB President Christine Lagarde recently highlighted the potential risks that Artificial Intelligence (AI) poses to financial stability, particularly in areas like financial market trading and cyber resilience.
title: ECB Monetary Policy and Eurozone Inflation Outlook
